svg.title: How narrowing teaches a type checker, shown as one value moving through two versions of the same function. Both start from a parameter annotated str or None, about which the checker knows only that it is either a string or None, so it refuses any string method on it. On the left the guard is missing: the function goes straight to name.upper(), the checker's knowledge has not changed, and it reports an error on that exact line — Item None of str or None has no attribute upper, with the error code union-attr — pointing at the use, not at the definition. On the right the guard is present: an if name is None branch returns early, and from the line after it the checker knows the only possibility left is str, so name.upper() is accepted and the file checks clean. The bottom of the diagram records that assert isinstance and an early raise narrow in exactly the same way, and that narrowing is ordinary readable Python that also happens to be the proof the checker needs.
svg.text: Narrowing: how a guard teaches the checker what it already told you
The same value, the same annotation, two versions of one function.
def greet(name: str | None) -> str:
what the checker knows about `name` right here:
str | None
so .upper() is refused — None does not have it
NO GUARD
GUARDED
line 8: return name.upper()
nothing has taught the checker anything,
so `name` is still str | None here
the error is reported HERE
fin.py:8: error: Item "None" of
"str | None" has no attribute
"upper" [union-attr]
line 8 — the use, not line 7, the definition
the annotation was fine; the missing guard was not
if name is None:
return "(anonymous)"
one possibility is handled and left behind
what the checker knows on every line below:
str
the union has one member left
return name.upper()
accepted, because .upper() exists on str
Success: no issues found in 1 source file
and the None case now has real behaviour
The same mechanism, spelled three ways
if x is None: return · assert isinstance(x, str) · if not isinstance(x, dict): raise ValueError(...)
Each one removes a possibility, and the checker follows the control flow to see that it is gone.
You are not writing code for the checker. You are writing the case you forgot, and the checker noticed.
